title: SYSK Live: The DB Cooper Heist
summary: Live recording at the Neptune Theater in Seattle, Washington, of Stuff You Should Know covering the 1971 D.B. Cooper skyjacking. Opens with Chuck's note that this is an archived live show from the previous year's tour, recorded before later developments in the case, followed by off-topic banter about sitting down to pee and a Movie Crush promo. The main content walks through the Northwest Orient Flight 305 hijacking from Portland to Seattle on Thanksgiving Eve 1971: the ransom demand, the crew's release and Tina McClough's exchange, the parachutes and money, the takeoff toward Mexico City route, the jump over the Cascades, and the FBI manhunt. It then covers the Cooper name mix-up, the 1980 Tena Bar money find, the 2008 parachute find, suspects including Richard McCoy, Dwayne Weber, Kenneth Christiansen, and L.D. Cooper, the Larry Carr evidence release, the aftermath changes to airline security, and the Boeing 727-style aft stair safety paddle. Sign-off follows.

segments.title: Movie Crush promo and archive intro
segments.summary: Chuck promotes a call for guests for his Movie Crush show, then introduces this archived live show about D.B. Cooper, recorded in Seattle and before later case developments.

segments.title: Opening banter at the Neptune Theater
segments.summary: Hosts open the live show in Seattle with off-topic banter about sweating, sitting down to pee, and restarting the podcast.

segments.title: Hijacking begins on Flight 305
segments.summary: Cooper buys a ticket at Portland airport for Flight 305 to Seattle on a Boeing 727-100 with a crew of five and about 37 passengers. He passes a note to flight attendant Florence Schaffner claiming a bomb and demanding $200,000, parachutes, and a fuel truck.

segments.title: Background on skyjacking and FBI policy
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the many hijackings of the era, the FBI's air marshal approach under J. Edgar Hoover, and why no marshal was on the flight.

segments.title: Negotiations, money, and parachutes
segments.summary: The plane circles Seattle-Tacoma while the FBI gathers $200,000 in marked twenties from a bank and parachutes from Seattle Sky Sports, where a dummy chute was mistakenly included. Tina McClough trades herself for the items and returns to the plane.

segments.title: Refueling, flight instructions, and the jump
segments.summary: Cooper sets flight instructions (altitude, flap setting, speed) and the rear stairs are lowered. The crew is released except Schaffner and the pilots. Around 8:01 p.m. the plane jolts, and Cooper is gone; the crew reports the jump around 8:13 p.m. The hosts recount the FBI's psychiatric profile and its nipple-fixation joke.

segments.title: Manhunt and early investigation
segments.summary: Jets and helicopters are sent after the plane, and the search focuses near the Lewis River and Ariel, Washington. The press leak turns Dan Cooper into D.B. Cooper, and the FBI keeps the error. Suspicious clues include the clip-on tie, cigarette butts, and a Dan Cooper comic.

segments.title: Ralph Himmelsbach and the 1980 Tena Bar money
segments.summary: Ralph Himmelsbach's theory that Cooper died in the jump is discussed, along with the weather and the freezing jump conditions. In 1980 Brian Ingram found several stacks of the ransom money on Tena Bar along the Columbia River.

segments.title: 2008 parachute find and suspects
segments.summary: A 2008 parachute found in Amboy, Washington, was identified by Earl Cossey as not Cooper's, but as belonging to a jet pilot, Floyd Walling. The hosts then review suspects Richard McCoy, Dwayne Weber, Kenneth Christiansen, and L.D. Cooper, including family claims.

segments.title: Larry Carr, evidence release, and legacy
segments.summary: Larry Carr, FBI agent in charge, is revealed as the poster 'Secret' on a skydiving forum and releases case evidence. The hijacking led to airport metal detectors, bag searches, and the aft stair paddle nicknamed the Cooper vane. The episode ends with the Ariel festival and sign-off.
